title: Discernment
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Discernment is the ability to test what is true, false, wise, foolish, good, and evil according to God’s Word. It is not suspicion or pride, but humble judgment shaped by Scripture and love for Christ.
summary: Discernment is the ability to test what is true, false, wise, foolish, good, and evil according to God’s Word. It is not suspicion or pride, but humble judgment shaped by Scripture and love for Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the truth, and discernment protects devotion to Him. Believers test teachings, desires, influences, and spiritual claims so they are not led away from the Gospel.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Discernment is necessary because not everything that sounds spiritual is true. Scripture calls believers to test the spirits, examine teaching, and hold fast to what is good.

Mature discernment is trained through use. Believers grow in the ability to distinguish good from evil as they are shaped by Scripture, prayer, obedience, and practice.

True discernment is humble. It does not produce arrogant criticism or fear-driven suspicion. It produces love that abounds with knowledge, purity, wisdom, and faithfulness to Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
False teaching, emotional pressure, cultural trends, and personal desire can all confuse believers. Without discernment, people may follow what sounds good rather than what is true.

This doctrine is especially important for vulnerable or hurting people who may be drawn to any voice promising quick relief. Discernment keeps them anchored in Scripture and Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Test what you hear, desire, believe, and follow by Scripture. Do not accept teaching simply because it is popular, emotional, impressive, or attached to a trusted personality. Seek humility, wisdom, and love for truth.
